summary: (2) Any person aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, may file a review petition on the following grounds within forty days of the making of such decision, direction, or order: (a) Upon the discovery of new and important matter or evidence that, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the direction, decision, or order was passed or; (b) On account of some mistake or error apparent from the face of the record, or; (c) If there is any other sufficient reason to review the matter. ” 14. The Review Petitioner has contended that the Commission had disallowed the time overrun of 85 days, i.e., time over-run of 59 days from 30.9.2022 to 28.11.2022 (delay due to transportation of 80 MVAR Bus reactor from Lucknow) and time over- run of 26 days from 11.1.2023 to 6.2.2023 (time taken for Application to CEA for Energisation to commissioning of the Subject Asset) in the impugned order and consequently disallowed the IDC and IEDC of ₹43.33 lakh on account of delay not condoned in the impugned order. 15. The Review Petitioner has further contended that the Commission did not consider the MoM of the 11th CMETS dated 30.9.2022, wherein the earlier approved 125 MVAR Bus Reactor was modified to 80 MVAR Bus Reactor in view of the transportation constraint and wherein it was recorded that the installation of the bus reactor could take two to three months. The Commission ought to have condoned the time overrun of 26 days for the period from 11.1.2023 to 6.2.2023 as the time was availed by the CEA for inspection and carrying out the necessary requirements for issuing the Energisation Certificate and the Review Petitioner had no control over the internal processes or timelines of the CEA. Therefore, the Review Petitioner had no control over the delay caused by the CEA. The Review Petitioner has also contended that the Commission had erred in disallowing the IDC & IEDC on account of delay not condoned and the events of the delay were beyond the control of the Petitioner. Order in Review Petition No. 20/RP/2025 Page 12 of 22 20. We have considered the submission of the Review Petitioner. As per the chronology of events submitted by the Review Petitioner, it is observed that the Review Petitioner has claimed the time overrun on the basis of delay in issuance of the Minutes of Meeting of the 11th CMETS held on 30.9.2022 (13 days), time lapsed in arranging internal approvals for award of contract for transportation (24 days), for issuance of bidding documents & subsequent LoA to the contractual agency M/S Kataria Carriers (10 days) and time taken by the contractual agency for commencement of transportation (12 days). 21. With regard to the time overrun of 13 days claimed by the Review Petitioner on account of delay in issuance of Minutes of Meeting (MoM) of the 11th CMETS held on 30.9.2022, it is noted that the Review Petitioner was a participant in the said meeting and, being a participant, was well aware of the discussions held in the meeting. it recorded in the said meeting that the Review Petitioner should make efforts to commission the asset by December 2022, in view of envisaged high voltage issues in the upcoming winter season. Therefore, we are of the view that the Review Petitioner ought to have proactively taken the necessary steps to transport the 80 MVAR Bus Reactor from Lucknow to Chamera Substation early, without waiting for the issuance of the Minutes of the Meeting of the aforesaid meeting on 13.10.2022. Accordingly, the 13-day delay due to the issuance of the MoM does not justify the delay in transporting the 80 MVAR Bus Reactor. Accordingly, the review on this count is rejected. 22.
